blocks.text: I can say what household chores we do and they do, and what chores we love and hate.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: A verb whose infinitive ends in -ar.
A verb whose infinitive ends in -er.
The form of the verb found in a dictionary. It gives the general meaning of the verb.
The -ing form of the verb that works as a noun in a sentence.

blocks.text: Sam y Jacob practican la pronunciación. Juegan a un juego: ‘Bingo’. Here are some of the words in their game.
Listening carefully to the sounds and writing the words you hear is called **transcribing**.
Reading and writing known and unknown words improves your pronunciation and your knowledge of {sound-spelling} correspondences.
Read each word aloud, then check your pronunciation. Listen carefully to every sound.
These words are useful for talking about las tareas del hogar (household chores).
To mean ‘we’ with an -ar verb, remove the **-ar** ending and add **-amos**.

rows.note: Ayudamos en el jardín. = We help in the garden.

blocks.text: To mean ‘they’ with an -ar verb, remove the **-ar** ending and add **-an**.

rows.note: Ayudan en la cocina. = They help in the kitchen.

blocks.text: With an -er verb, remove the **-er** ending. For ‘we’ add **-emos**. For ‘they’ add **-en**.

rows.note: Hacemos la cama. = We make the bed.

blocks.q: Listen to the verb ending. Is it ‘we’ or ‘they’?

slides.title: Love and hate: amar and odiar

blocks.text: To say we or they **love** or **hate** doing something, use amar or odiar. After it, use the **infinitive**.

items: Amamos {lavar} el suelo. = We love washing the floor.
Aman {lavar} el suelo. = They love washing the floor.
Odiamos {preparar} comida. = We hate preparing food.
Odian {preparar} comida. = They hate preparing food.

blocks.text: We change the ending of amar or odiar to say who loves or hates. The verb that follows stays in the {infinitive}.
In English we can translate amar + infinitive word for word, with ‘to + verb’ (the infinitive).

items: Odio correr. = I hate to run.
Amo cocinar. = I love to cook.

blocks.text: But we usually use the gerund (the -ing form): I hate running. I love cooking.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: In Spanish, these verbs are always followed by the **infinitive**. Do not use an -ing form in Spanish.

options: After amar or odiar we use the infinitive.
After amar or odiar we use the -ing form (gerund).
We never change the ending of amar or odiar.
blocks.why: We change amar or odiar to say who loves or hates, but the verb that follows is in the infinitive.

slides.title: Say what we love and hate

items.q: We love washing the clothes: Amamos ___ la ropa.
They hate tidying up the toys: Odian ___ los juguetes.

blocks.q: An opinion says what people love or hate. An activity says what people do.

items: Reading and writing known and unknown words improves pronunciation and knowledge of sound-spelling correspondences.
‘We’ with an -ar verb: remove -ar and add **-amos**. ‘They’: remove -ar and add **-an**.
‘We’ with an -er verb: remove -er and add **-emos**. ‘They’: remove -er and add **-en**.
To say we love or hate doing something, use the ‘we’ form of amar or odiar, then the **infinitive**. In English this is often the -ing form.

flashcards.front: How do you say ‘we’ with an -ar verb?
flashcards.back:
Remove the -ar ending and add -amos.

tirar → tiramos (we throw)

flashcards.front: How do you say ‘they’ with an -ar verb?
flashcards.back:
Remove the -ar ending and add -an.

tirar → tiran (they throw)

flashcards.front: How do you say ‘we’ with an -er verb?
flashcards.back:
Remove the -er ending and add -emos.

comer → comemos (we eat)

flashcards.front: How do you say ‘they’ with an -er verb?
flashcards.back:
Remove the -er ending and add -en.

comer → comen (they eat)

flashcards.front: What is the infinitive of a verb?
flashcards.back: The form of the verb found in a dictionary. It gives the general meaning of the verb.
The -ing form of the verb that works as a noun in a sentence.

flashcards.front: Which verb form follows amar or odiar in Spanish?
What does ‘Amamos lavar el suelo’ mean?
What do lavar and ordenar mean?
flashcards.back:
lavar = to wash, washing
ordenar = to organise, to tidy up

flashcards.front: What do el juguete, la ropa and el suelo mean?
flashcards.back:
el juguete = the toy
la ropa = the clothes, clothing
el suelo = the floor

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Household chores: -ar and -er verbs ‘we’ form
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a short answer. Write the Spanish words in lower case.

questions.prompt: Write the ‘we’ form of the verb tirar (to throw).
questions.explanation: Remove the -ar ending and add -amos: tir + amos.

questions.prompt: Write the ‘they’ form of the verb comer (to eat).
questions.explanation: Remove the -er ending and add -en: com + en.

questions.prompt: Write the ‘we’ form of the verb limpiar (to clean).
questions.explanation: Remove the -ar ending and add -amos: limpi + amos.

questions.prompt: Write the ‘they’ form of the verb ordenar (to tidy up).
questions.explanation: Remove the -ar ending and add -an: orden + an.

questions.prompt: Write the ‘we’ form of the verb hacer (to make, to do).
questions.explanation: Remove the -er ending and add -emos: hac + emos.

questions.prompt: Write in Spanish: ‘we love washing the car’.
questions.explanation: Use the ‘we’ form of amar (amamos), then the infinitive (lavar).

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with the infinitive of lavar: ‘Odian ___ el suelo.’ (They hate washing the floor.)
questions.explanation: After odiar we always use the infinitive.

questions.prompt: Write in English: ‘Ayudamos en el jardín’.
accepted: we are helping in the garden
questions.explanation: Ayudamos is the ‘we’ form of ayudar (to help).

questions.prompt: Write in English: ‘Aman lavar el suelo’.
accepted: they love to wash the floor
questions.explanation: Aman is the ‘they’ form of amar. In English we can use -ing or ‘to + verb’.
